transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Uh, yeah… I came in because I’m not really eating right anymore. Like, some days I just have coffee, maybe a piece of bread if it’s there. My pants are getting loose on me, like hanging off kind of.

I used to keep things in the kitchen, you know, simple stuff, but then I’ll start thinking about needing to go to the store and how the prices are now, and I just don’t end up doing it. But mostly, yeah… I’m not eating much, and I’m losing weight.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess down is one word for it. Most days when I wake up, it’s like there’s this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest, like nothing good is waiting for me. I end up just wanting to keep my head down.

It’s weird, ’cause I’ll think about stuff I used to do, or even just going outside, and then my mind wanders to other things, like the neighbors making noise or bills sitting there, and I just… I don’t know, I lose the point of doing anything.
Have you lost interest in activities or things you used to enjoy doing?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I used to like walking by the lake, just kind of looking at the water, you know? And I had these little model kits I’d work on, tiny pieces and all that… I’d sit there for hours sometimes.

Now they’re just sitting there. I look at them like they belong to somebody else. Like, I know I used to care about them, but I can’t really get myself to start. And the lake too, I think about going, then I just… don’t.
Would you say that most days, you feel depressed or down most of the day?

Yeah… most days, yeah. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything, it’s more like I wake up and there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like before I even get out of bed, it feels like nothing good is waiting for me.

Sometimes I’ll just stare at the wall, and then I start thinking about stupid little things, like the mail piling up or how the floor needs sweeping, and then I forget what I was even trying to do. But yeah… most of the day I just want to keep my head down.
Have you had this depressed or empty feeling for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yeah… it’s been most days. I mean, I don’t keep a calendar or anything—my kitchen one’s still on the wrong month, actually—but when I wake up, it’s that same heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like nothing good’s waiting for me.

And it kind of stays there, you know? I just keep my head down and get through the day, or try to.
Can you tell me if you’ve had days where you feel down or lose interest in things, along with problems like trouble sleeping, feeling tired, or thinking about yourself in a negative way?

Yeah… the sleep part, definitely. Lately I’ll go to bed and just lie there for hours, staring at the wall, like my body’s tired but it won’t shut off. There’s this little crack in the paint near the window I keep looking at, and then I start thinking I should fix it, but I don’t.

Other times I wake up before the sun’s even up and I can’t get back to sleep. I just lay there waiting for the day to start, I guess. And even when I do sleep some, I still feel worn out, like it didn’t count.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you needed less sleep or your thoughts raced, even if it was for just a few days?

Yeah… there was a time like that, I guess. Right after I got fired, I didn’t feel crushed at first, weirdly. I felt kind of… fired up, like nobody could touch me, like maybe they’d done me a favor or something.

But I was also real quick to snap. If somebody said, “maybe slow down” or tried to calm me down, I’d get mad fast. My brother said something like that once while we were standing by his truck, and I just remember the sun was in my eyes and I was thinking about how dirty the windshield was instead of listening to him… but yeah, I got sharp with people. Like I couldn’t stand being told to ease up.
Did that fired-up, irritable period last for four days or longer, or did it fade more quickly?

It didn’t just fade in a day or two, no. It’s hard for me to pin it down cleanly because everything kind of ran together after I got fired… like one week I’m up and driven and mad at everybody, and then it’s like I fell through the floor.

That whole scary swing—from that fired-up feeling to being this low—has been going on about a month, I think. Maybe around there.
Have you had three or more separate periods in your life where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you needed less sleep or your thoughts raced?

Three or more… I don’t know. I’m trying to count it, but it’s not like I wrote it down anywhere. There were times I got wound up or people said I was acting different, but whether that was three separate times… I can’t say for sure.

I remember little pieces more than the whole thing, like where I was standing or what somebody said, but then the actual number of times gets fuzzy. So… I don’t know how to answer that cleanly.

Can you think back and tell me if there were at least three different times in your life when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you needed less sleep or your thoughts were racing?

I’m trying to think of it like separate times, but my head doesn’t sort it that way. Like, I can remember being in certain places, or somebody looking at me funny, or me pacing around, but then whether that was one “time” or another “time”… I don’t know.

Three sounds like a lot when you say it that way. Maybe? I really can’t say for sure. My memory kind of grabs onto weird little details instead of the count.

Can you think back and tell me if there were at least three different times in your life when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you needed less sleep or your thoughts were racing?

I mean, the one I can really point to is right after I got fired. I felt… fired up, like nobody could really touch me, like I knew what I was doing and everybody else was in my way.

But then if someone told me to slow down, or acted like I was being too much, I’d snap at them fast. Like my temper was right there. I keep thinking about that day and how people were looking at me, but as far as three different times… I still don’t know how to count it.

Can you think back and tell me if there were at least three different times in your life when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you needed less sleep or your thoughts were racing?

I know I keep circling this, but the main one I can actually remember is right after I got fired. I was like… charged up, like nobody could touch me, and I was sure everybody else was just in my way.

But then if someone said, “Slow down,” or looked at me like I was doing too much, I’d snap real quick. Like, just sharp with people. I can picture that more than I can count how many separate times it happened.

Can you recall if there were at least three different times in your life when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you needed less sleep or your thoughts were racing, each lasting at least several days?

Yeah, I hear you saying “three” and “several days,” and that’s where I get stuck. I don’t want to just make up a number.

The one I keep coming back to is right after I got fired. I felt really fired up, like… untouchable, like people needed to get out of my way. And then if somebody told me to slow down, I’d get irritated quick, snap at them. I remember that feeling real clear.

But three separate times, lasting days each… I can’t really sort it that clean in my head.
Can you think back and tell me if you’ve had at least three different times in your life when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, each time lasting for several days in a row?

I don’t know if I can honestly say three separate times. The one I keep thinking about is after I got fired. I was really fired up, like… kind of untouchable, like I knew what I was doing and everybody else was just in the way.

And then if someone told me to slow down, I’d snap at them quick. Like, I’d get irritated fast. I remember that part clear, but counting it out into three different stretches for several days… I get mixed up with that.

Can you think back and tell me if you’ve had at least two more separate times in your life when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, each lasting several days in a row, outside of the time right after you were fired?

Outside of getting fired… I’m trying to think, but it all kind of blends together for me. That one is the one that sticks out, because I was really fired up, like I couldn’t be stopped, and people telling me to slow down just made me snap at them.

I mean, I’ve had times where people got on my nerves, sure, but two more separate times for several days like that… I can’t really pull them apart in my head. That fired one is the clear one.

Can you think back and tell me if you’ve ever had another time in your life, besides after you were fired, when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you needed less sleep or your thoughts were racing, lasting for several days in a row?

I’m trying to think of another one, but honestly the one that keeps coming up is still after I got fired. I felt… fired up, like nobody could tell me anything, kind of untouchable. And when people said I needed to slow down, I’d snap at them real fast.

Other than that, I don’t know. My memory gets messy with stuff like that. Like I can remember the feeling, but not clean enough to say, “yeah, that was another several-day stretch.”

Can you think back and tell me if you’ve ever had another time in your life, besides after you were fired, when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, lasting for several days in a row?

I’m trying to think, but I keep circling back to the same one, right after I got fired. That was the time I felt really fired up, like kind of untouchable, like people didn’t know what they were talking about.

And if anybody told me I should slow down, I’d snap at them fast. I mean, I don’t know why people always think saying “calm down” helps, because it just makes you more mad, you know? But another separate time like that for several days… I’m not sure I can say that clear. That fired one is the one I remember.

Can you think back and tell me if you’ve ever had another time in your life, besides after you were fired, when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, lasting for several days in a row?

I know you’re asking besides that time, but I keep landing on the same thing. Right after I got fired, I was all charged up, like… I don’t know, untouchable almost. Like nobody could tell me nothing.

And if somebody said I needed to slow down, I’d snap real quick. I remember that clear because people kept acting like they knew better, and that just set me off. But another separate time like that for days… I can’t really pull one out.

Can you think back and tell me if you’ve ever had another time in your life, besides after you were fired, when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, lasting for several days in a row?

Yeah, I know you keep asking besides that, but that’s the one I keep coming back to. Right after I got fired, I felt really fired up, like nobody could touch me, like people were just in my way.

And then if somebody said, “you need to slow down,” I’d snap at them quick. I’d get mad fast, like, who are you to tell me what to do? But another whole separate time like that… I don’t know, my mind kind of jumps around when I try to pin it down.

Can you think back and tell me if you’ve ever had another time in your life, besides after you were fired, when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, lasting for several days in a row?

I get what you’re asking, like another time besides that, but I keep ending up back there. Right after I got fired, that’s when I felt all fired up, like nobody could touch me, like I knew what was what and everybody else was just talking.

And then if people told me to slow down, I’d snap fast. Like real quick, I’d get mad. I know that’s the one I already said, but that’s the one that sticks out. Another separate stretch like that… I’m not really pulling one up right now.
